definition: Paradigms of AI Programming: Case Studies in Common Lisp (ISBN 1-55860-191-0) is a well-known programming book by Peter Norvig about artificial intelligence programming using Common Lisp.
details: Paradigms of AI Programming: Case Studies in Common Lisp (ISBN 1-55860-191-0) is a well-known programming book by Peter Norvig about artificial intelligence programming using Common Lisp.

explainer.lead: Paradigms of AI Programming: Case Studies in Common Lisp is a well-known programming book by Peter Norvig about artificial intelligence programming using Common Lisp. It matters as a teaching text that builds AI techniques through worked programs.

tiers.eli5: It is a book that teaches AI by having you write real programs, one case study at a time, in the Lisp language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers read it to learn classic AI techniques through case studies implemented in Common Lisp. A practical caveat is that it assumes familiarity with Lisp, which is uncommon in mainstream engineering stacks.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a book (ISBN 1-55860-191-0) by Peter Norvig on AI programming using Common Lisp, structured as case studies. Being a text, it states no formal definition of its own.

explainer.example: A reader works through a case study, implementing the described AI program in Common Lisp as the book presents it.
